newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS - JUNE 19.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS - JUNE 19.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek financial press:

--Management and a 40 percent stake in the state-run casino on Mt. Parnes will be offered to the private sector after an international tender, in line with proposals by Development Minister Vasso Papandreou to be discussed at today's Cabinet meeting. The Mt. Parnes package includes an offer for the transfer of the casino to Athens after a year. A new Athens casino, according to estimates, would generate turnover of 300 billion drachmas annually and profits before tax of 60 billion.

--An experts' report on government economic policies to be released today recommends a strict incomes policy for the private and public sectors until the country achieves Maastricht convergence criteria.

--The privatisation of state-run paper mills Softex was resolved yesterday after two months of negotiations when 11 creditor banks yesterday said they would grant the enterprise a 3.9 billion drachma loan to keep it open until it was sold.

--The government's attention is now turning to the course of inflation as National Economy and Finance Minister Yannis Papandoniou cautioned that although the economy had covered two-thirds of the way to Maastricht, there could be no slackening of economic policy. Inflation may have fallen to 5.4 percent but it has stalled and the ministry believes that it will be exceptionally difficult to get it to the forecast goal of 4.5 percent.
--The state is to establish a registered company to handle, monitor and best exploit the stakes it holds in banks, public enterprises and organisations.

--The Greek telecoms organisation OTE second share offer and the privatisation programme will bring in 260 billion drachmas, according to reports. Next on the list for privatisation is Cretabank and the Bank of Central Greece and the public offer for Duty-Free Stores and the Athens Stock Exchange.

--The European Commission yesterday gave OTE until 2001 to lift its monopoly on the telecommunications market in Greece. Greece had asked to wait until January 2003 for full liberalisation but the EU exectuive noted that a plan to modernise and digitalise the network should be completed by the end of 2000.
--Papandoniou yesterday left open the option of index-linking tax brackets to inflation, saying that the government was aware of the inequalities in the existing system.
--The casino on the island of Syros is facing problems, just a month and a half after it opened. Initial figures of revenues for the April-May period have fallen short of projected targets.

--The pulic debt is 670 billion drachmas over initial projections for 1997, according to the half-yearly report from the national economy ministry. The figure is now projected at 35.668 billion drachmas (109 percent of GDP), from the original forecast of 35.0000 billion drachmas (107.2 percent). Servicing of the public debt however, thanks to the quick de-escalation of interest rates, will be 160 billion drachmas less this year.

--Government and unions clashed for the first time yesterday over plans to change the social security and pensions system. Public and private sector unions are demanding the abolition of a 1992 law due to go into effect in 1998 but Labour Minister Miltiades Papaioannou rejected the demand.

--The environment, town planning and public works ministry yesterday said it expected Olympic Metro, the consortium construction the Athens subway system, to deliver the project on time. So far, however, the project is lagging, with only 58 percent of the project completed and delivery date November 1998.
